item.text:
**7B.9 research note: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 2024**

Overall, I found a mixed record. There is real evidence of rules-based procurement and some transparent/technocratic appointments, but also clear patronage and information-control caveats. I did not find solid 2024 evidence on pardons/clemency specifically.

**Positive claims**
- **Contract integrity rules for big procurement** — [Controladoria-Geral da União](https://www.gov.br/cgu/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2024/12/dia-internacional-de-combate-a-corrupcao-presidente-lula-assina-decreto-que-fortalece-integridade-em-contratos-publicos), 2024-12-09. Claim: Lula signed a decree requiring large federal contractors to implement integrity programs, with CGU monitoring compliance and integrity used in bid tie-breaks. This supports anti-patronage, anti-corruption procurement controls. Question IDs: `7B.9`.
- **Public-access channel for presidential speech records** — [Secretaria de Comunicação Social](https://www.gov.br/secom/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/perguntas-frequentes/onde-posso-acessar-discurso-e), 2024-03-21. Claim: the government directs the public to official transcripts, audio, and video archives of Lula’s speeches. This supports access to public information rather than secrecy or informal gatekeeping. Question IDs: `7B.9`.
- **Technocratic central-bank appointment** — [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/brazils-lula-to-nominate-galipolo-as-cenbank-chief-says-finance-minister-3591764), 2024-08-28. Claim: Lula picked Gabriel Galípolo, then a sitting central-bank monetary policy director and former finance-ministry official, and Reuters reported Galípolo’s continuity/freedom-of-decision framing. This points more toward competence-based appointment than loyalist patronage. Question IDs: `7B.9`.

**Negative claims**
- **Cabinet patronage/capture caveat** — [Reuters via UOL](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/06/12/ministro-das-comunicacoes-e-indiciado-pela-pf-por-corrupcao-em-investigacao-sobre-desvio-na-codevasf-dizem-fontes.htm), 2024-06-12, and [Reuters via UOL](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/06/13/lula-diz-que-tomara-decisao-sobre-juscelino-filho-e-que-indiciamento-nao-significa-que-ministro-cometeu-erro.amp.htm), 2024-06-13. Claim: Communications Minister Juscelino Filho was formally indicted in a Codevasf-related corruption probe, and Lula did not immediately remove him. This is the clearest 2024 patronage/capture warning sign relevant to appointments and public resources. Question IDs: `7B.9`.
- **Pressure on information environment** — [Reuters Institute](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/brazil), 2024-06-17. Claim: the justice minister threatened an hourly fine when Google opposed the government’s fake-news bill. That is a real pressure signal on public-information access, even if framed as anti-disinformation. Question IDs: `7B.9`.
- **State pressure to remove allegedly false health content** — [Agência Gov / Planalto](https://agenciagov.ebc.com.br/noticias/202412/apos-notificacao-do-governo-federal-youtube-retira-conteudo-falso-sobre-saude-do-presidente-lula), 2024-12-16. Claim: after an AGU notice, YouTube removed videos alleging false claims about Lula’s health. This may be defensible anti-disinformation policy, but it is still direct state pressure on information flow and a cautionary item for the access-to-information side of the lens. Question IDs: `7B.9`.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a credible 2024 source showing Lula using pardons/clemency in a clientelist or retaliatory way, nor a solid counterexample proving clean, patronage-free behavior in that area. The evidence base I found is strongest for procurement, appointments, and information control.
